from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Turbulence is an energy cascade of chaotic fluid motion.",
            "Inertial forces dominate at high velocities.",
            "Viscous forces eventually dampen the flow motion."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Chaos in the Fluid", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visuals
        turbulent_field = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color=BLUE).shift(self.grid[f"{r}{c}"])
            for r in "BCDEF" for c in "3456"
        ])
        
        turbulence_label = Text("Turbulence", color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(turbulence_label, "B2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(turbulent_field), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(Write(turbulence_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        particles = VGroup(*[Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["C4"]) for _ in range(10)])
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), FadeIn(particles))
        self.play(*[
            p.animate.move_to(self.grid[f"{chr(ord('C')+i%3)}{3+i%4}"]) 
            for i, p in enumerate(particles)
        ], run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        dissipation_zone = Rectangle(color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.3, width=2, height=2)
        self.place_in_area(dissipation_zone, "D3", "E5")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), FadeIn(dissipation_zone))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy cascades from large scales to small.",
            "Small-scale turbulence is isotropic and universal.",
            "Governed by dissipation rate and viscosity."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Kolmogorov Hypotheses (1941)", lecture_lines)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Structure: The Energy Spectrum", [
            "Energy follows the Kolmogorov -5/3 spectrum.",
            "Wavenumber k relates to eddy scale size.",
            "The spectrum shows power density versus wavenumber.",
            "Energy cascades down across these scales.",
            "This structure reveals underlying mathematical order."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex("E(k) \\propto k^{-5/3}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F1C40F")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 2], y_range=[-3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        axes.scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        graph = axes.plot(lambda k: -1.66 * k, x_range=[-0.5, 1.5], color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3498DB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        highlight_term = MathTex("k^{-5/3}", color="#F1C40F", font_size=36)
        highlight_term.move_to(formula[0][4:])
        self.play(Indicate(highlight_term))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#9B59B6")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Kolmogorov Length Scale (η)", [
            "Viscosity turns kinetic energy into heat.",
            "Eta is the smallest turbulence length scale.",
            "Formula: η equals ν cubed over ε."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        eta_dot = Dot(color=BLUE)
        formula = MathTex(r"\eta = \left( \frac{\nu^3}{\varepsilon} \right)^{1/4}", font_size=42)
        exponent = formula.get_part_by_tex("1/4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_at_grid(eta_dot, "C3", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(eta_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.place_in_area(formula, "D2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(exponent, color="#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-world Application", [
            "Energy enters large and dissipates at η.",
            "Constants enable modeling without tracking atoms.",
            "Turbulence models help design efficient systems."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Atmospheric turbulence vs pipe flow side by side
        atm = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=BLUE).add(Text("Atmosphere", font_size=16))
        pipe = Rectangle(width=2, height=2, color=YELLOW).add(Text("Pipe Flow", font_size=16))
        
        side_by_side = VGroup(atm, pipe).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(side_by_side, 'B1', 'D6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(side_by_side))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Summarize K41 utility with a checkmark icon
        checkmark = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color="#2ECC71").scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, 'E3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(checkmark))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out all with a summary message 'Understanding Chaos'
        summary_text = Text("Understanding Chaos", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(*self.mobjects),
            Write(summary_text)
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

sections.title: Introduction: The Chaos in the Fluid
sections.content: Define turbulence as a multi-scale energy cascade. Introduce the concept of the Reynolds Number (Re) as the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces, determining the transition from laminar to turbulent flow.
sections.example: Visualize a calm stream transitioning into a chaotic whitewater rapid as the velocity (inertial force) increases.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Hypotheses (1941)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Scale Invariance' principle. Explain that at small scales, turbulence is isotropic and governed solely by the energy dissipation rate (ε) and kinematic viscosity (ν).
sections.example: Animation of a large swirling vortex (eddies) breaking down into smaller and smaller vortices, resembling a fractal tree structure.

sections.title: Mathematical Structure: The Energy Spectrum
sections.content: Present the Kolmogorov -5/3 Power Law. Use a log-log plot to show the spectral energy density E(k) as a function of wavenumber k. Explain that k represents the inverse of eddy size.
sections.example: A visual graph where a straight line with a -5/3 slope emerges from a sea of data points, illustrating how energy 'cascades' down the scales.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Length Scale (η)
sections.content: Define the smallest scale where viscosity finally dominates and kinetic energy is converted into heat. Provide the formula η = (ν³/ε)^(1/4). Explain that this is the 'floor' of the mathematical structure.
sections.example: An animation of a tiny robotic submarine (nano-drone) struggling to navigate against the friction of these micro-vortices.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Recap the cascade: Energy enters at large scales and dissipates at scale η. Emphasize that these constants allow us to model weather, aircraft drag, and industrial mixing without needing to track every single atom.
sections.example: A falcon adjusting its wings in turbulent wind; the bird instinctively navigates the energy cascade to maintain stability.
